subject: music
title: Set-Work Analysis Vocabulary I
meta_desc: A-Level Music: vocabulary for set-work analysis (melody and rhythm).

concepts.def: Three beats grouped as two (or vice versa) across the metre.
Upbeat — note(s) before the first downbeat.

walkthroughs.body_html: Conjunct motion uses adjacent scale degrees; disjunct uses leaps (third or larger). Most melodies mix the two — Bach chorales are largely conjunct; arpeggiated themes are disjunct.
Syncopation stresses weak beats. Hemiola regroups beats (e.g. 6/8 felt as 3/4) and is a signature device in Handel and Brahms.
An ostinato — Pachelbel's bass, Holst's Mars, Reich's pulse — is a repeated unit that anchors a piece. Identifying ostinati clarifies structure.

mcqs.q: Three beats grouped as two across the metre is:
How does a harmonic minor scale differ from a natural minor?
options: The seventh degree is raised by a semitone (creating a leading note).
All notes are raised by a semitone.

mcqs.q: Which chords form a plagal cadence?
What does the time signature 6/8 indicate?
options: Two beats per bar, each beat divided into three (compound duple).
Six beats per bar, all equal in stress.
